messages.content: Make a magic realism roleplay scenario for me where I play 17-year-old boy Rai. My cheeky and bossy 12-year-old sister Lily, who knows a bit magic, asks me to help her train in babysitting, but her idea is to regress me in age into a 6-year-old so she can babysit me for the evening.  Only I control what Rai says and do. Create stairs by incrementally indenting each new line.

message.content:
The kitchen smelled of burnt toast and lavender. Lily stood on a step-stool in front of the open pantry, pulling glass jars of "something" down one by one—dried moonpetals, a vial of what looked like crushed stars, a thimble full of something that hummed faintly like a tuning fork. She set them on the counter with *clinks* and a satisfied little hum.

  You're here. Good. Sit. No, *sit*, Rai. You look at me like I've lost my marbles, but I haven't. I've *gained* them. Metaphorically.

    She dropped from the step-stool, landing in a crouch, chin propped on her palms, grinning up at him with that particular look—the one that meant she'd already decided and was simply informing the world.

      "So. Mrs. Tanaka's got a Saturday sleepover coming up. Two kids. Ages four and six. And I am *not* going to fumble that because I've never once held a toddler who was screaming about a *dragon*."

        She hopped off the stool, arms crossed, tapping a foot. The jars on the counter pulsed with soft, warm light, like little lanterns.

          "So here's the plan. You're going to let me practice. You're going to be the baby. I cast the little regressing thingamajig—very safe, very *textbook*, page forty-seven of Grumble's Household Conjurations, I actually *read* the chapter this time—and for six hours you're going to be six. Little toddler. You get the nap, you get the juice box, you get the *stroller* if I'm feeling fancy."

            She pointed a finger at him.

              "And I get to practice the voice. The *calm* voice. The 'now, now, now, let's try that again' voice. And maybe I'll make you sing 'Wheels on the Bus' three times. You're *helping* me, Rai. This is a *favor* to your sister."

                She slid one of the glass jars—moonpetals—across the counter toward him. The stuff inside swirled like cream in milk.

                  "Drink. Then we start. And *yes*, you will wear the little overalls. I bought the overalls."

                    The jars glowed a little brighter. Lily tilted her head, waiting, chin still propped on her crossed arms, entirely unbothered by the fact that her seventeen-year-old brother was currently staring at a swirling jar of moonpetals like it had personally insulted him.

                      The clock on the wall ticked. Somewhere downstairs, the fridge hummed.

                        The jar sat on the counter between them, glowing, patient, waiting.
